headline: John Jumper joins Anthropic after 9 years at Google DeepMind
summary: Ex-Google DeepMind researcher John Jumper to join Anthropic
details: John Jumper, a researcher who led the AlphaFold team at Google DeepMind, is leaving the company after nearly 9 years to join Anthropic. He expressed gratitude to Demis Hassabis for taking a chance on him. Jumper will be joining Anthropic after taking some time off to recharge.
Jumper's departure from Google DeepMind and his move to Anthropic marks a significant change in his career. During his time at Google DeepMind, he played a crucial role in leading the AlphaFold team.

The reasons behind Jumper's decision to leave Google DeepMind and join Anthropic are not explicitly stated. However, his move to Anthropic is expected to bring new perspectives and expertise to the company.

What happens when a leading AI researcher leaves Google DeepMind?

John Jumper, a researcher who led the AlphaFold team at Google DeepMind, is leaving the company after nearly 9 years to join Anthropic. He expressed gratitude to Demis Hassabis for taking a chance on him. Jumper will be joining Anthropic after taking some time off to recharge.

Jumper's departure from Google DeepMind and his move to Anthropic marks a significant change in his career. During his time at Google DeepMind, he played a crucial role in leading the AlphaFold team.

headline_marked: Companies [[reining in AI usage]] as costs strain budgets
headline: Companies reining in AI usage as costs strain budgets
summary: AI costs are straining company budgets, leading to reduced usage
details: Companies are reining in their AI usage as the costs of implementing and maintaining the technology strain their budgets. This shift is happening across various industries as businesses assess the financial impact of AI on their operations.

The costs associated with AI, including development, deployment, and maintenance, have proven to be higher than anticipated for many companies. As a result, businesses are reassessing their AI strategies to ensure they align with their financial capabilities.

The trend of reduced AI usage highlights the challenges companies face in integrating AI into their operations while managing costs. It also underscores the need for more cost-effective AI solutions that can provide a better return on investment.
caption:
Can companies afford AI? Costs are straining budgets

Companies are reining in their AI usage as the costs of implementing and maintaining the technology strain their budgets. This shift is happening across various industries as businesses assess the financial impact of AI on their operations.

The costs associated with AI, including development, deployment, and maintenance, have proven to be higher than anticipated for many companies. As a result, businesses are reassessing their AI strategies to ensure they align with their financial capabilities.

The trend of reduced AI usage highlights the challenges companies face in integrating AI into their operations while managing costs. It also underscores the need for more cost-effective AI solutions that can provide a better return on investment.
